title: The herdr executor behind the five operations
description:
The herdr executor: the five operations, and nothing about herdr above them.

Implement Executor for herdr behind the SAME interface Phase 1 defined
(internal/reconcile/reconcile.go:57): Start, Inspect, CollectDetail, Cancel,
Dispose. All herdr-specific addressing lives inside JobHandle.handle, the one
open object in the contract (internal/exec/subprocess/record.go:218-223). The
reconciler must learn nothing about panes, workspaces or protocols.

Design rules, from the Phase 1 retro:
- THE VERDICT LIVES IN DURABLE EVIDENCE, NEVER IN THE SUBSTRATE. Phase 1's
  executor decides from a report on disk, commits on a branch, and an exit code,
  and refuses to read process chatter as liveness. This one inherits that.
  ticks' own collect package is the proof it works: collect.go:108-109 makes
  zero herdr calls, so herdr cannot touch a verdict by construction. Keep that
  property.
- The substrate goes in PROVENANCE. Records already carry executor, model and
  profile digest; add the herdr protocol and server version, so a run that spans
  an upgrade can be diagnosed rather than guessed at.
- Do NOT port ticks' spawn/wait/reconcile/cleanup packages. ticfac's reconciler
  already owns waves, adoption, disposition and cleanup. Only the herdr-specific
  parts belong here: Start is agent.start plus worktree/workspace creation,
  Inspect is agent.get plus durable evidence, Cancel is the stop, Dispose is the
  teardown. Read those four ticks packages for the hard-won details (the
  pane-busy retry, the readiness poll, the refusal to tear down on an unanswered
  agent.list) and carry the LESSONS, not the code.
- Resume across an upgrade is the first hazard to design for: a job started
  under one protocol that a later leg cannot address is HELD for a person and
  never redispatched — the old worker may still be alive and spending.
acceptance_criteria: A herdr Executor implements Start, Inspect, CollectDetail, Cancel and Dispose; the reconcile package contains no herdr-specific code and the Executor interface is unchanged; all herdr addressing lives inside JobHandle.handle; the verdict is derived from the report and the branch and never from a herdr call, asserted by a test that answers every herdr query with an error and still collects the right verdict; every record a herdr dispatch produces carries the herdr protocol and server version in its provenance; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
